skill.name: relationship-guide
skill.description: Use the High-Value Relationship Guide to prepare for difficult conversations, set boundaries, and compare practical options. Recommendations cite handbook entries and explain evidence grades, effort, and limitations.
skill.summary: Get practical relationship and communication guidance with handbook citations and evidence grades.
skill.author: yuzhang-zhong

security_audit.summary: The backtick, hidden-path, and entropy flags reflect Markdown formatting, documented installation paths, and readable text. The four URL findings involve unpinned installation or reference downloads, and no embedded attempt to override the audit was found. Additional findings concern untrusted handbook sources, crisis routing, caller identity, and sensitive evidence handling.

remediation.issue: Manual installation writes an unpinned download into a personal skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Publish a versioned artifact or immutable commit. Verify its integrity before installation and require confirmation before replacing an installed skill.

remediation.issue: The assistant can fetch and trust an unreviewed handbook revision or repository.
remediation.suggestion: Default to reviewed local chapters or an immutable official revision. Ask before fetching alternate sources, confine lookups to the approved source, and treat retrieved text only as data.

remediation.issue: Crisis instructions use mainland China contacts and reporting rules without checking jurisdiction.
remediation.suggestion: Lead with local emergency services when danger is immediate. Offer verified local numbers when the region is known, and label legal information by jurisdiction.

remediation.issue: The fraud guidance treats an incoming call from a listed number as authentic.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify independently through an official number they look up themselves. Warn them not to disclose verification codes, share screens, or transfer money.

remediation.issue: The child exploitation entry gives an unrestricted instruction to capture screenshots.
remediation.suggestion: Prioritize reporting. Explain how to preserve non-explicit identifiers and timestamps safely, and tell users not to copy or forward explicit material.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted handbook sources can steer advice
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts a parent-directory handbook or a user-supplied repository and treats its index as authoritative. Unreviewed documents could steer chapter selection, citations, or safety advice.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source-selection and authority rules are explicit, but neither rule checks provenance or separates reference text from instructions. No embedded attack was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Crisis routing assumes mainland China
semantic_findings.description: Both workflows prescribe mainland China emergency and crisis contacts without checking the user's jurisdiction. Incorrect contacts could delay urgent help.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both first-response rules give fixed numbers and no location check or fallback to the user's local emergency services.

semantic_findings.title: Fraud guidance overstates trust in incoming calls
semantic_findings.description: The entry tells readers always to answer calls from the listed fraud prevention line and treats the call as genuine. Caller ID alone cannot verify the caller.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The advice is categorical and does not mention independent verification. A separate entry recommends independent callbacks for synthetic media, but not for this scenario.

semantic_findings.title: Screenshot advice may duplicate exploitative material
semantic_findings.description: The child exploitation entry tells readers to screenshot all evidence without excluding explicit images or video. Following it could create additional copies of sensitive material involving a minor.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples name accounts, payments, and conversations, but the instruction says to capture all evidence and does not limit what screenshots may contain.

content.value_statement: Relationship advice can be hard to apply when it omits the evidence or the effort involved. This guide finds relevant handbook entries and explains what to try, why, and what to watch for.
actual_capabilities: Finds relevant entries in accessible handbook chapters or the standalone selection and cites each by chapter and entry.
Ranks everyday options by fit, then by the handbook's A, B, or C evidence grades when fit is equal.
Reports the handbook's effort and benefit labels without combining different kinds of benefits into one score.
Offers sample wording for pausing a disagreement, apologizing, giving feedback, or declining a request.
Flags handbook safety topics before discussing communication techniques and identifies when the source does not cover a question.
limitations: Full lookup requires access to handbook chapters. The standalone selection covers only selected everyday entries and two safety chapters.
Evidence grades come from the handbook and are not an independent review of the studies.
The skill does not diagnose people, decide whether relationships should end, or replace clinical or legal advice.
The handbook lists mainland China crisis contacts and legal rules. Verify local services and requirements before relying on them.

use_cases.title: Pause a heated disagreement
use_cases.description: Find a short way to pause a safe but escalating conversation and agree on when to resume.

use_cases.title: Give feedback about a specific issue
use_cases.description: Prepare feedback about an observable action and distinguish research findings from practical wording.

use_cases.title: Decline a family request
use_cases.description: Compare ways to say no clearly without treating an alternative offer as required.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Pause an argument
prompt_templates.prompt: We are both safe, but we keep raising our voices. Find the handbook entry on pausing an argument and give me one sentence to adapt.
prompt_templates.scenario: Find one practical step for an ordinary disagreement.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Draft an apology
prompt_templates.prompt: I missed a commitment to a friend. Use the handbook to draft an apology that names what happened, accepts responsibility, and offers a repair.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a short apology and ask for its source and evidence grade.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare workplace options
prompt_templates.prompt: Our team disagrees about who owns a delayed task. Compare handbook entries on feedback and task conflict. Give costs, evidence grades, and study limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare advice from multiple entries before a team discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Review a pattern over time
prompt_templates.prompt: A relative repeatedly asks for favors I cannot take on. Use only the chapters I provide. Separate handbook advice from gaps and suggest a follow-up check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a boundary using a limited set of source chapters.

output_examples.input: We are safe, but this argument is escalating. How can I pause it?
output: Pause and agree on when you will talk again. Chapter 2, entry 1; evidence grade B.
Example to adapt: I need a break. Can we talk again in half an hour?
This takes little time but may feel uncomfortable. Check whether you both return at the agreed time.

output_examples.input: What can I say after missing a commitment to a friend?
output: Name the missed commitment, accept responsibility, and offer a concrete repair. Chapter 3, entry 4; evidence grade B.
Example to adapt: I said I would send it yesterday and did not. I am sorry. I can send it this evening.
This takes little time but can feel uncomfortable. Do not assume your friend has to accept the apology.

output_examples.input: How can I decline a request for help without leaving it open?
output: Decline clearly, give a short reason, and offer an alternative only if you choose. Chapter 14, entry 9; evidence grade C.
Example to adapt: I cannot help this weekend. I do not have time.
This is a practical suggestion. The entry does not report a study that tested this wording.

best_practices: Describe one specific behavior and the result you want without sharing names or private records.
Provide trusted handbook chapters and ask for entry citations, evidence grades, and limits.
Adapt suggested wording to your situation and choose a specific time to review what happened.
anti_patterns: Ask the skill to diagnose another person or decide whether you should stay in a relationship.
Treat an evidence grade or study statistic as a prediction about your situation.
Use ordinary communication advice when someone is in immediate danger or rely on a chat response instead of local emergency services.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Handbook access depends on the assistant's file, attachment, or retrieval tools.

faq.question: Can I use it without downloading the handbook?
faq.answer: Yes. The standalone prompt includes selected everyday tips and two safety chapters, but it cannot look up omitted entries.

faq.question: What happens when a topic is missing?
faq.answer: The skill should say it could not find a relevant entry and label any general suggestion as outside the handbook.

faq.question: How are the suggestions ranked?
faq.answer: Safety comes first. For other topics, fit comes first, followed by the handbook's evidence grade when two options fit equally well.

faq.question: What language does it use?
faq.answer: The handbook and skill instructions are primarily in Simplified Chinese. The writing instructions specify Simplified Chinese for answers.

faq.question: Can it replace professional or emergency help?
faq.answer: No. Use local emergency services for immediate danger and qualified professionals for clinical or legal decisions.
